requirements.statement: A user must sign in to the app, and their todos persist privately across sessions and devices.

criteria.must: An unauthenticated visitor opening the app is presented a sign-in flow before any todo content is shown
After a user successfully signs in, the system shows that user's own todos and lists
When a signed-in user signs out, the system ends their session and returns them to the sign-in flow
If a user's session has expired, the system requires them to sign in again before performing any todo operation

requirements.statement: A user can create a new todo item with a title, and optionally a description and due date.

criteria.must: Submitting a new todo with a non-empty title creates the todo and displays it in the user's todo list
Submitting a new todo with an empty title is rejected and a validation message is displayed
Creating a todo allows an optional description to be provided at creation time
Creating a todo allows an optional due date to be provided at creation time
A newly created todo's initial status is incomplete

requirements.statement: A user can view their todos and organize them into lists.

criteria.must: Opening the app displays all of the signed-in user's todos, grouped by list
Creating a new list with a non-empty name adds the list and allows todos to be assigned to it
Moving a todo from one list to another updates its list association and the change is reflected immediately
When a user has no todos, an empty-state message is displayed instead of an empty list
Filtering todos by status (all, active, completed) displays only todos matching the selected filter

requirements.statement: A user can edit an existing todo's details.

criteria.must: Editing a todo's title, description, or due date and saving persists the changes and displays the updated todo
Attempting to save a todo with an empty title is rejected and a validation message is displayed
Cancelling an in-progress edit discards unsaved changes and retains the todo's previous values

requirements.statement: A user can mark a todo complete or reopen it, and see overdue todos indicated.

criteria.must: Marking an incomplete todo as complete updates its status and visually distinguishes it from incomplete todos
Marking a completed todo as incomplete reopens it and restores it to the active list
A todo whose due date has passed and is still incomplete is visually indicated as overdue

requirements.statement: A user can delete todos and lists they no longer need.

criteria.must: Deleting a todo removes it from the user's todo list permanently
Requesting to delete a todo prompts for confirmation before it is deleted
Deleting a list that contains todos moves those todos to a default list or prompts the user for how to handle them, rather than silently deleting the todos

requirements.statement: A user's todos and lists are private and persist durably.

criteria.must: Requesting todos returns only todos and lists owned by the requesting user
An attempt to access or modify another user's todo or list is denied
A todo change (create, edit, complete, delete) persists so it survives sign-out and sign-in on a different session
